animation.init: AVL tree with {{count}} value(s). BF (balance factor) = height(left) - height(right), and every node must stay between -1 and +1
animation.ins_left: {{val}} < {{curr}}, so go to the left child
animation.ins_right: {{val}} > {{curr}}, so go to the right child
animation.ins_equal: {{val}} already exists, so its count becomes {{count}} and the tree shape does not change
animation.ins_place_root: The tree is empty, so {{val}} becomes the root
animation.ins_place: There is nothing to the side, so {{val}} is placed as a new leaf under {{parent}}
animation.bf_check: Back at node {{node}}: height = {{height}}, BF = height(left) - height(right) = {{bf}}
animation.balanced: BF {{bf}} is within -1 to +1, so node {{node}} stays as it is
animation.unbalanced_ll: Node {{node}} has BF {{bf}} and its left child {{child}} leans left (BF {{childBf}}): a left-left (LL) case, one right rotation fixes it
animation.unbalanced_lr: Node {{node}} has BF {{bf}} and its left child {{child}} leans right (BF {{childBf}}): a left-right (LR) case, rotate the child left first, then the node right
animation.unbalanced_rr: Node {{node}} has BF {{bf}} and its right child {{child}} leans right (BF {{childBf}}): a right-right (RR) case, one left rotation fixes it
animation.unbalanced_rl: Node {{node}} has BF {{bf}} and its right child {{child}} leans left (BF {{childBf}}): a right-left (RL) case, rotate the child right first, then the node left
animation.rotate_child_left: Call node.left ← RotateLeft(node.left): rotate {{node}} to the left, so its right child {{pivot}} will move up and the shape becomes a left-left line
animation.rotate_child_right: Call node.right ← RotateRight(node.right): rotate {{node}} to the right, so its left child {{pivot}} will move up and the shape becomes a right-right line
animation.rotate_right: Call RotateRight on {{node}}: its left child {{pivot}} is going to become the root of this subtree. Watch the pointers change one by one
animation.rotate_left: Call RotateLeft on {{node}}: its right child {{pivot}} is going to become the root of this subtree. Watch the pointers change one by one
animation.ins_done: Inserting {{val}} is complete and every node is balanced again
animation.rot_right_pivot: x ← y.left: label the node being rotated, {{node}}, as y and its left child, {{pivot}}, as x. Nothing has moved yet
animation.rot_right_move: y.left ← x.right: y now points to x's old right subtree T2 (root {{t2}}) as its left child. T2 is briefly linked from both x and y
animation.rot_right_move_empty: y.left ← x.right: x has no right subtree, so y's left child becomes empty
animation.rot_right_link: x.right ← y: y becomes the right child of x, which replaces the link to T2
animation.rot_right_height_node: UpdateHeight(y): y = {{node}} now sits lower, and its height becomes {{height}}
animation.rot_right_height_pivot: UpdateHeight(x): x = {{pivot}} is now above y, and its height becomes {{height}}
animation.rot_right_return: Return x: {{pivot}} is the new root of this subtree, and the parent now points to it instead of {{node}}
animation.rot_left_pivot: y ← x.right: label the node being rotated, {{node}}, as x and its right child, {{pivot}}, as y. Nothing has moved yet
animation.rot_left_move: x.right ← y.left: x now points to y's old left subtree T2 (root {{t2}}) as its right child. T2 is briefly linked from both y and x
animation.rot_left_move_empty: x.right ← y.left: y has no left subtree, so x's right child becomes empty
animation.rot_left_link: y.left ← x: x becomes the left child of y, which replaces the link to T2
animation.rot_left_height_node: UpdateHeight(x): x = {{node}} now sits lower, and its height becomes {{height}}
animation.rot_left_height_pivot: UpdateHeight(y): y = {{pivot}} is now above x, and its height becomes {{height}}
animation.rot_left_return: Return y: {{pivot}} is the new root of this subtree, and the parent now points to it instead of {{node}}
animation.del_empty: The tree is empty, so there is nothing to delete
animation.del_compare: Compare the value to delete, {{val}}, with node {{curr}}
animation.del_left: {{val}} < {{curr}}, so look in the left child
animation.del_right: {{val}} > {{curr}}, so look in the right child
animation.del_not_found: {{val}} is not in the tree, so nothing is deleted and the tree stays as it is
animation.del_count_dec: {{val}} is stored several times, so only its count drops to {{count}} and the node and the tree shape stay the same
animation.del_leaf: {{val}} has no children (a leaf), so it can simply be removed
animation.del_one_child: {{val}} has a single child, {{child}}, so {{child}} takes its place
animation.del_remove_leaf: Leaf {{val}} is removed and the matching pointer of its parent becomes empty
animation.del_remove_child: {{val}} is removed and its parent now points straight to {{child}}
animation.del_two_child: {{val}} has two children, so it cannot just be cut out. Find its successor (the smallest value in the right subtree) to take its place
animation.del_succ_find: Successor candidate is {{succ}}, which still has a left child, so keep going left
animation.del_succ_found: {{succ}} has no left child, so it is the successor (the smallest value in the right subtree)
animation.del_succ_copy: node.value ← successor.value: the node that held {{val}} now stores the successor's value {{succ}} (with its count). The original successor node is removed next
animation.del_succ_remove_leaf: node.right ← RemoveMin(node.right): remove the successor node {{succ}}. It has no right child, so its place becomes empty
animation.del_succ_remove_child: node.right ← RemoveMin(node.right): remove the successor node {{succ}}, and its right child {{child}} takes its place
animation.del_done: Deleting {{val}} is complete and every node along the path is balanced again
animation.need_balance: Some nodes are out of balance (shown in red), and insert and delete assume the tree is balanced already. Press Rebalance first
animation.chk_empty: The tree is empty, so there is nothing to check
animation.chk_ok: BF {{bf}} is within -1 to +1 and the subtrees are balanced too, so {{node}} returns left And right = True
animation.chk_bad: BF {{bf}} is outside -1 to +1, so {{node}} is unbalanced and returns False
animation.chk_done_ok: Every node has a BF between -1 and +1, so the tree is balanced
animation.chk_done_bad: Check complete: {{bad}} node(s) are unbalanced (in red). Press Rebalance to fix them
animation.rb_already_empty: The tree is empty, so there is nothing to rebalance
animation.rb_already: Every node has a BF between -1 and +1, so the tree is already balanced and nothing changes
animation.rb_done: Rebalancing is complete and every node has a BF between -1 and +1 again
animation.rot_missing: {{val}} is not in the tree, so it cannot be rotated
animation.rot_blocked_left: {{val}} has no right child to move up, so it cannot be rotated left
animation.rot_blocked_right: {{val}} has no left child to move up, so it cannot be rotated right
animation.rot_select: Node {{val}} is selected for the rotation
animation.rot_done: Rotation complete: {{pivot}} took the place of {{val}}. A rotation never breaks the ordering, but BF values can change (unbalanced nodes turn red)
animation.srch_empty: The tree is empty, so {{val}} cannot be found
animation.srch_compare: Compare the value to find, {{val}}, with node {{curr}} (node number {{steps}})
animation.srch_left: {{val}} < {{curr}}, so look in the left child
animation.srch_right: {{val}} > {{curr}}, so look in the right child
animation.srch_not_found: There is no node on that side, so {{val}} is not in the tree ({{steps}} node(s) compared)
animation.chk_call: Call IsBalanced({{node}}) (level {{depth}}): the node is not Null, so check its subtrees first
animation.chk_null_left: The left child of {{parent}} is empty: IsBalanced(Null) returns True right away
animation.chk_null_right: The right child of {{parent}} is empty: IsBalanced(Null) returns True right away
animation.chk_go_left: left ← IsBalanced({{node}}.left): check the left subtree of {{node}} first
animation.chk_go_right: right ← IsBalanced({{node}}.right): the left subtree is done, now the right one
animation.chk_bf: Both subtrees are checked, so now {{node}} itself: height {{height}}, BF = {{bf}}
animation.chk_ok_child_bad: The BF {{bf}} of {{node}} is within -1 to +1, but a subtree holds an unbalanced node, so left And right = False and that goes back to the caller

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: An AVL tree is a **binary search tree that rebalances itself**. After every insertion or deletion it checks the height of each subtree and rotates nodes so the tree never leans too far to one side.
items: **Balance factor (BF)**: height of the left subtree minus height of the right subtree
**AVL rule**: every node must have a BF of [[primary|-1, 0 or +1]]
A plain BST can degrade into a linked list; the AVL rule keeps the height at [[success|O(log n)]]
The same ordering rule as a BST still holds: left is smaller, right is larger

sections.heading: Rotations
sections.content: When a node's BF becomes +2 or -2, a rotation restores the balance without breaking the BST ordering.
items: **Right rotation (LL case)**: the left child becomes the new root of the subtree
**Left rotation (RR case)**: the right child becomes the new root of the subtree
**Left-right (LR) and right-left (RL)**: rotate the child first, then the node
Each rotation changes only a few pointers, so it takes [[success|O(1)]] time

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Because the height stays logarithmic, every operation stays fast even in the worst case.
items: **Search, insert, delete**: [[success|O(log n)]] in the worst case
An insertion needs **at most one rebalancing** (one or two rotations)
A deletion may rotate on **several levels** on the way up

sections.heading: Things to Watch
sections.content: AVL trees trade a little extra work on writes for predictable reads.
items: The tree is stricter than a red-black tree, so it **rotates more often** but is slightly shallower
Duplicate values are counted on the existing node, like the BST level
Loaded data is built as a plain BST in the order you typed it and can be unbalanced, so rebalance it before inserting or deleting
